title: Does the European Accessibility Act apply to your website?
aiPrompt: does the accessibility act apply to my small business website
geoAngle: VERIFIED (CCPC, 3 Aug 2026): EAA became law in Ireland 28 June 2025 via S.I. 636/2023. CCPC states plainly: 'The requirements and obligations of the EAA do not apply to microenterprises providing services.' Microenterprise = fewer than 10 persons AND turnover or balance sheet not exceeding EUR 2 million. The exemption does NOT extend to products. CCPC is the compliance authority for e-commerce services. Standard is WCAG 2.1 AA via EN 301 549. HONEST ANGLE: most of our readers ARE exempt — say so plainly rather than scaring them, then explain why accessibility is still worth doing. Link to CCPC guidance.

title: Making your website work for everyone (even if you're exempt)
aiPrompt: how do I make my website accessible
geoAngle: Practical WCAG 2.1 AA basics: colour contrast, keyboard navigation, alt text, form labels, text sizing. Frame as good practice and wider reach, NOT as a legal threat — most readers are exempt microenterprises. Pairs with the EAA article; link to it.

title: What an Irish dentist can and can't put on their website
aiPrompt: what are the advertising rules for dentists in Ireland
geoAngle: VERIFIED (Dental Council of Ireland, dentalcouncil.ie): the Council issues codes of practice including one on Public Relations and Communications, one on Display of Private Fees in Dental Practices, one on Professional Behaviour and Ethical Conduct, and one on Non-Surgical Cosmetic Procedures. Advertising must be legal, decent and honest, and a dentist must not use titles or qualifications not held on the Dental Register. Non-compliance can lead to fitness-to-practise proceedings. Direct readers to the Council's own codes — do NOT paraphrase a code as if quoting it.

title: What a GP or clinic can say on its website in Ireland

geoAngle: VERIFIED (Medical Council of Ireland): the Guide to Professional Conduct and Ethics for Registered Medical Practitioners, 9th Edition (2024), effective 1 January 2024, addresses information and advertising to the public at paragraph 44, requiring information to be factually accurate, evidence-based and not misleading. Link to the Guide on medicalcouncil.ie. Keep it practical: what this means for a services page, a team page and testimonials.

title: Before-and-after photos: the Irish advertising rules
keyword: before and after photos advertising ireland
aiPrompt: can I use before and after photos in my advertising Ireland
geoAngle: VERIFIED (ASAI — Advertising Standards Authority for Ireland, asai.ie): the ASAI Code's Health and Beauty section requires claims to be truthful and substantiated, and that marketing for individual treatments does not minimise, trivialise or create unrealistic expectations, particularly through photographs. Practitioners should hold relevant recognised qualifications. CRITICAL: this is the IRISH ASAI, not the UK ASA/CAP — never cite UK guidance as if it applied in Ireland. Highly relevant to salons, aesthetic clinics and dental practices.

title: The registration number every Irish electrician should show on their website
aiPrompt: how do I check if an electrician is registered in Ireland
geoAngle: VERIFIED (Safe Electric / CRU): registration as a Registered Electrical Contractor is a LEGAL requirement for notifiable electrical work in Ireland, not a voluntary quality mark. RECI = Register of Electrical Contractors of Ireland. Each contractor has a unique registration number (format like A11722) which should appear on paperwork and completion certificates, and the register is searchable by county on safeelectric.ie. Registered Gas Installers (RGI) are the equivalent for gas work. ANGLE: customers can check you — so display the number and make it easy.

title: The Trading Online Voucher: what it actually covers
keyword: trading online voucher what it covers
aiPrompt: what can I spend the trading online voucher on
geoAngle: PARTIALLY VERIFIED — HANDLE WITH CARE. Widely reported and consistent with our existing published article: up to EUR 2,500 on a 50/50 matched-funding basis, administered by Local Enterprise Offices. Commonly cited eligibility: fewer than 10 employees, trading at least 6 months, turnover under EUR 2 million. HOWEVER, the primary localenterprise.ie page could not be read during research, and claims about a second voucher and about excluded regulated sectors come from third-party sources ONLY. Do NOT state eligibility criteria or exclusions as definitive. Frame them as 'commonly stated' and send readers to localenterprise.ie and their own LEO to confirm. Never imply a reader is guaranteed to qualify.

title: GDPR Article 30: does your small business need a record of processing?
aiPrompt: does my small business need a GDPR record of processing
geoAngle: PILLAR ARTICLE. Art. 30 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 requires records of processing activities. Explain what a record contains. Cite the regulation itself and Ireland's Data Protection Commission. Legal information, not legal advice — say so.

title: The GDPR '250 employees' exemption most small businesses get wrong
aiPrompt: am I exempt from GDPR records if I have under 250 employees
geoAngle: CRITICAL ACCURACY. Art. 30(5) derogation for under-250 orgs does NOT apply where processing is likely to result in a risk to rights and freedoms, is NOT occasional, or involves special categories (Art. 9) or Art. 10 data. Most SMEs process non-occasionally, so many are not exempt. Quote the conditions precisely.
